points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 诺姆·乔姆斯基1928年出生于费城一个犹太裔家庭。他的父亲威廉·乔姆斯基是希伯来语学者，母亲艾尔西·乔姆斯基是来自乌克兰的移民。乔姆斯基从小就展现出对语言和知识的浓厚兴趣，阅读了大量书籍，包括希伯来语经典和文学作品。这段时期的教育经历为他后来的学术思想奠定了基础，特别是他对语言结构和政治批判的早期关注。
points.descriptionEn: Noam Chomsky was born in 1928 in Philadelphia to a Jewish family. His father William Chomsky was a Hebrew scholar, and his mother Elsie Chomsky was an immigrant from Ukraine. From an early age, Chomsky showed a keen interest in language and knowledge, reading extensively including Hebrew classics and literary works. This formative educational period laid the foundation for his later academic ideas, particularly his early focus on language structure and political critique.

points.title: 学术启蒙
points.description: 乔姆斯基进入宾夕法尼亚大学，主修数学、语言学和哲学。在此期间，他受到哲学家尼尔森·古德曼的影响，开始对语言结构产生浓厚兴趣。1951年，他完成了硕士论文《现代希伯来语的语音结构》，并开始发展其转换生成语法理论。这段时期的研究成果为他后来在语言学的革命性突破奠定了基础，同时也培养了他对政治和社会问题的批判性思维。
points.descriptionEn: Chomsky attended the University of Pennsylvania, majoring in mathematics, linguistics, and philosophy. During this time, he was influenced by philosopher Nelson Goodman and developed a strong interest in language structure. In 1951, he completed his master's thesis 'The Morphophonemics of Modern Hebrew' and began developing his theory of transformational generative grammar. This period of research laid the foundation for his later revolutionary breakthroughs in linguistics while also cultivating his critical thinking about political and social issues.

points.title: 语言学革命
points.description: 乔姆斯基加入麻省理工学院(MIT)语言学系，并在此完成了他最具影响力的著作《句法结构》(1957)。这本书提出了转换生成语法理论，彻底改变了语言学研究的范式。他认为语言能力是人类与生俱来的天赋，而非简单的习惯养成。这一时期，乔姆斯基还积极参与反战运动，发表了对美国外交政策的尖锐批评，开始了他在政治领域的活跃生涯。他的语言学理论与政治批判思想在这一时期相互影响，形成了独特的学术与政治双重身份。
points.descriptionEn: Chomsky joined the MIT Department of Linguistics and completed his most influential work 'Syntactic Structures' (1957). This book introduced the theory of transformational generative grammar, revolutionizing the paradigm of linguistic research. He argued that language ability is an innate human faculty rather than merely learned behavior. During this period, Chomsky also became active in anti-war movements, publishing sharp critiques of U.S. foreign policy, beginning his prominent career in political activism. His linguistic theories and political critique mutually influenced each other during this time, forming his unique dual identity as scholar and political critic.

points.title: 学术与政治巅峰
points.description: 乔姆斯基继续在MIT任教，同时深化了他的语言学研究和政治批判。1969年，他发表《美国权力与新模式》，系统分析了美国外交政策的帝国主义本质。1971年，他出版《无政府状态、国家与乌托邦》，与自由主义哲学家罗伯特·诺齐克展开著名辩论。这一时期，他发表了大量关于媒体、政治和全球化的著作，如《制造共识》(1988)与《必要的幻觉》(1989)。乔姆斯基建立了'认知科学'项目，将语言学与其他学科融合，同时成为全球反战、反全球化运动的思想领袖，影响了无数进步主义者和活动家。
points.descriptionEn: Chomsky continued teaching at MIT while deepening his linguistic research and political critique. In 1969, he published 'American Power and the New Mandarins,' systematically analyzing the imperialist nature of U.S. foreign policy. In 1971, he released 'Anarchism, State, and Utopia,' engaging in a famous debate with liberal philosopher Robert Nozick. During this period, he published numerous works on media, politics, and globalization, including 'Manufacturing Consent' (1988) and 'Necessary Illusions' (1989). Chomsky established the 'Cognitive Science' program, integrating linguistics with other disciplines, while becoming an intellectual leader of global anti-war and anti-globalization movements, influencing countless progressives and activists.

points.title: 晚年影响
points.description: 进入21世纪，乔姆斯基继续活跃于学术和政治领域。他发表了《霸权还是生存》(2003)、《失败的国家》(2006)等著作，进一步批判美国的外交政策。2017年，他与政治经济学家罗伯特·波尔共同出版《制造共识：政治经济中的大众媒体控制》。尽管年事已高，乔姆斯基仍频繁发表演讲和文章，参与公共辩论，成为知识界最具影响力的声音之一。他的理论影响了人工智能、认知科学和政治学等多个领域，同时他的政治观点持续激励着全球范围内的进步运动。乔姆斯基被广泛认为是当代最具影响力的公共知识分子之一。
points.descriptionEn: Entering the 21st century, Chomsky remained active in both academic and political spheres. He published 'Hegemony or Survival' (2003) and 'Failed States' (2006), further critiquing U.S. foreign policy. In 2017, he co-authored 'Manufacturing Consent: The Political Economy of the Mass Media' with political economist Robert Pollin. Despite his age, Chomsky continues to frequently give lectures and write articles, participating in public debates as one of the most influential voices in intellectual circles. His theories have influenced multiple fields including artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and political science, while his political perspectives continue to inspire progressive movements worldwide. Chomsky is widely regarded as one of the most influential public intellectuals of our time.

supporter.zh: 乔姆斯基被支持者誉为20世纪最具原创性和影响力的思想家之一。他在语言学领域的革命性理论彻底改变了人们对语言本质的理解，提出了人类具有先天语言能力的观点。作为政治评论家，他坚持批判美国外交政策的帝国主义本质，揭露媒体如何服务于权力结构，为全球反战和正义运动提供了重要思想武器。乔姆斯基的学术严谨性与道德勇气相结合，使他成为知识分子的典范，激励着几代追求真理和正义的人。
supporter.en: Chomsky is hailed by supporters as one of the most original and influential thinkers of the 20th century. His revolutionary theory in linguistics completely transformed our understanding of the nature of language, proposing the idea of an innate language faculty in humans. As a political commentator, he has consistently critiqued the imperialist nature of U.S. foreign policy and exposed how media serves power structures, providing crucial intellectual tools for global anti-war and justice movements. Chomsky's combination of academic rigor and moral courage makes him a model of intellectual integrity, inspiring generations of truth-seekers and justice advocates.

critic.zh: 批评者认为乔姆斯基的政治分析过于简化，常常采用阴谋论视角解释国际关系，忽视复杂的地缘政治现实。在语言学领域，他的理论被认为过于强调普遍语法而忽视了语言习得的认知过程和文化因素。一些学者指责他选择性使用证据，支持自己的预设观点。此外，他被批评为对共产主义政权的暴行缺乏同等程度的谴责，显示出政治立场的双重标准。这些批评者认为乔姆斯基的声誉部分来自于他迎合了西方知识界的反主流情绪，而非完全基于客观分析。
critic.en: Critics argue that Chomsky's political analysis is overly simplistic, often employing conspiracy-theory perspectives to explain international relations while ignoring complex geopolitical realities. In linguistics, his theory is criticized for overemphasizing universal grammar while neglecting the cognitive processes and cultural factors in language acquisition. Some scholars accuse him of selectively using evidence to support his predetermined views. Additionally, he has been criticized for failing to condemn communist regimes with the same intensity as Western powers, showing apparent double standards. These critics suggest that Chomsky's reputation stems partly from his appeal to the counter-mainstream sentiments of Western intellectuals rather than being based solely on objective analysis.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，乔姆斯基被定义为一位罕见的跨越学术与政治领域的公共知识分子。他的语言学理论已成为现代语言学的基石，而他的政治著作则成为批判性媒体研究的经典文本。乔姆斯基代表了冷战后期至今西方知识界对权力结构的持续批判传统，影响了从反全球化运动到占领华尔街等众多社会运动。在流行文化中，他既是学术明星也是政治偶像，其形象经常出现在纪录片和媒体中，成为反抗权威的象征。乔姆斯基的持久影响力在于他成功地将深奥的学术理论与通俗易懂的政治分析相结合，使复杂的思想能够广泛传播。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Chomsky is defined as a rare public intellectual who bridges academic and political spheres. His linguistic theories have become cornerstones of modern linguistics, while his political works have become classic texts in critical media studies. Chomsky represents the tradition of sustained critique of power structures in Western intellectual thought from the late Cold War to the present, influencing numerous social movements from anti-globalization to Occupy Wall Street. In popular culture, he is both an academic star and political icon, frequently appearing in documentaries and media as a symbol of resistance to authority. Chomsky's enduring influence lies in his successful combination of sophisticated academic theory with accessible political analysis, enabling complex ideas to reach wide audiences.

self.zh: 如果人类历史是一部关于战争、屠杀、压迫、剥削和残酷的记录，那么它也是一部关于反抗、牺牲、勇气、同情和创造力的记录。
self.en: If the history of the human race is a record of war, slaughter, oppression, exploitation, and cruelty, it is also a record of courage, sacrifice, endurance, sympathy, and creativity.

others.zh: 乔姆斯基是我们这个时代最伟大的知识分子之一，他不仅改变了我们对语言的理解，也改变了我们思考政治的方式。
others.en: Chomsky is one of the greatest intellectuals of our time, who has not only changed our understanding of language but also the way we think about politics.
